metaDescription: What happens after you get in touch, what I need from you, and how to choose materials and finishes for fitted furniture in London.
title: How it works,
lede: What I need from you, what you get from me, and the choices worth thinking about before we meet. Five minutes here saves a lot of back and forth.

steps.title: Get in touch
steps.description: Send photos and rough sizes on WhatsApp, or book a visit online. I reply within 24 hours.

steps.title: Survey
steps.description: I visit, measure every wall and talk through how you'll use the space.

steps.title: Draw
steps.description: You get a 3D drawing with real measurements. We adjust it until it's right, then you sign it off.

steps.title: Build
steps.description: Every panel is cut to that drawing, in 18 mm board throughout, backs included.

steps.title: Fit
steps.description: I fit it on site, scribed to your walls, floor and ceiling, and leave the room clean.

needIntro: Rough is fine. I measure everything properly at the visit. This just means I turn up with the right ideas.

need.title: Photos of the space
need.description: The whole wall from the doorway, then close-ups of anything in the way: sockets, switches, radiators, pipes, the boiler, skirting and coving.

need.title: Rough sizes
need.description: Width, height from floor to ceiling, and how far it can come into the room. A photo of the wall with the numbers written on it is perfect.

need.title: What it is for
need.description: What goes inside: long coats or shirts, folded clothes, shoes, books, a TV, files. A quick list helps more than anything.

need.title: A look you like
need.description: Two or three pictures from Pinterest or Instagram, or one of my jobs. It tells me more than any description.

need.title: Your area and access
need.description: Your area or postcode, which floor, stairs or lift, and where a van can park. In London that last one matters.

need.title: Budget and timing
need.description: A rough figure and when you would like it done, so I can suggest the right materials from the start.

get.title: A reply within 24 hours
get.description: To every enquiry, on WhatsApp, phone or email.

get.title: A free quote and a visit
get.description: I come and measure up, talk through how you will use the space and what is possible.

get.title: A 3D drawing to approve
get.description: With real measurements. We change it until it is right, and nothing is cut until you sign it off.

get.title: Built in 18 mm board
get.description: Throughout, backs included. No thin 8 mm sheets.

get.title: Fitted to your room
get.description: Scribed to your walls, floor and ceiling, with the room left clean when I go.

materialsIntro: Most fitted furniture is made from one of these. Not sure? Pick "not sure" in the brief below and I will suggest what suits the room and the budget.

materials.name: Painted MDF
materials.bestFor: Painted wardrobes, alcove units, bookcases, panelled doors.
materials.description: Smooth and stable, so it takes paint well and stays flat. Any colour you like. It needs painting: by me, or left ready for your decorator.
materials.imageAlt: White painted alcove unit with shelves and a cupboard

materials.name: Moisture-resistant MDF
materials.bestFor: Bathrooms, utility rooms, anywhere with steam or splashes.
materials.description: The green board. Worked the same way as normal MDF, but copes far better with damp. Painted like normal MDF.
materials.imageAlt: Cream painted vanity unit with brass handles

materials.name: Birch plywood
materials.bestFor: A natural wood look, modern rooms, desks and kids' rooms.
materials.description: Strong and light in colour, and the layered edge looks good left on show. Usually finished clear, so the grain shows.

materials.name: Walnut and oak
materials.bestFor: Desks, shelves and pieces you want to stand out.
materials.description: Real hardwood character and the richest look, at the highest cost. It often works best where you see and touch it most, like a desk top.
materials.imageAlt: Floating walnut desk under a window

materials.name: IKEA PAX, built in
materials.bestFor: Big wardrobes on a tighter budget.
materials.description: IKEA frames and fittings inside, built in with MDF tops and end panels up to the ceiling and finished with painted doors, so it looks fitted, not flat-pack.
materials.imageAlt: Full wall of built-in PAX wardrobes with painted doors

costNote: £ to ££££ shows how the materials compare with each other. It is not a price: every job is quoted on its own.

finishes.title: Painted
finishes.description: Any colour. Painted by me, or left ready for your decorator if you would rather they did it with the walls.

finishes.title: Natural wood
finishes.description: A clear finish on birch ply, oak or walnut, so the grain shows.

finishes.title: Doors
finishes.description: Hinged or sliding. Flat, panelled with moulding, glazed, or a grille over a radiator.

finishes.title: Handles
finishes.description: Knobs, long pulls, brass, or none at all, with a finger pull underneath like the walnut desk.

finishes.title: Inside
finishes.description: Rails, shelves, drawers, shoe space, strip lights. Tell me what goes in and I plan the inside around it.

briefIntro: Tick what fits and add sizes if you have them. Then send it to me on WhatsApp or by email, and add your photos in the chat.
briefUses: Hiding a boiler, radiator or cylinder

faq.question: Do you fit kitchens?
faq.answer: No. I build fitted furniture: wardrobes, alcove units, bookcases, window seats, desks and storage. I do build the pieces around a kitchen, like pantry cupboards and panelling.

faq.question: Do I need to clear the room?
faq.answer: Just the wall and some floor space in front of it. I put dust sheets down and leave the room clean.

faq.question: Can you work with IKEA PAX?
faq.answer: Yes. Building PAX in with tops, end panels and proper doors is a good way to get a fitted wardrobe for less. There are a few PAX jobs on My Work.

faq.question: Who paints it?
faq.answer: Either works. I can paint it, or leave it ready for your decorator. We agree which before I start.

faq.question: Can I change things after the drawing?
faq.answer: Yes, that is what the drawing is for. We change it until it is right. Once you sign it off, that is what gets built.

faq.question: Where do you work?
faq.answer: Across London, from Chiswick to East Finchley, and further out when the job suits.
